entries.title: JWST/NIRISS-SOSS Spectroscopic Variability and Auroral Modelling of Warm Ultracool Dwarf LSR J1835+3259
entries.abstract: Auroral variability in ultracool dwarfs (UCDs) has been proposed as a key source of optical and infrared modulation, yet its physical origin remains poorly understood. We present JWST Near Infrared Imager and Slitless Spectrograph/Single Object Slitless Spectroscopy (NIRISS/SOSS) time-series spectroscopy of the M8.5 UCD LSR J1835+3259. These observations probe the object's wavelength-dependent rotational variability, providing insight into the atmospheric processes underlying its infrared behaviour. Additional GTC/MEGARA optical spectra reveal that its H$α$ emission has declined markedly since earlier epochs, suggesting a reduced activity state during the JWST observations. We detect no emission from H$_3^+$ or absorption by hydronium in the NIRISS spectra. We use principal component analysis to identify two distinct modes of spectral variability: one dominated by FeH modulation near 1 $μ$m and another contributing broadband variability across the H and K bands. We find that no model atmosphere grid provides a reasonable fit to the average NIRISS spectrum. However, a blended model comprising an M-dwarf photosphere and a cooler blackbody component provides an improved fit to the mean spectrum, the broadband spectral energy distribution and the NIRISS broadband variability. By adding perturbations to PICASO model grids, we demonstrate that a combination of atmospheric heating and non-equilibrium chemistry can successfully mimic a blend of unperturbed photosphere and a blackbody, and that the presence of these effects may explain the unusual spectrum and variability of LSR J1835+3259.

entries.title: Properties of near-surface turbulence in hot, massive stars: Statistical signatures from multi-dimensional models of O-type stars
entries.abstract: Variability of massive stars indicates the presence of complex, multi-D physics near the surface. Recent advancements in multi-D radiation-hydrodynamical modelling of massive star atmospheres show strong turbulence triggered by the iron opacity bump. We analyze statistical properties of sub-surface turbulence in multi-D simulations of O-star atmospheres. Particularly, we study potential dependencies of turbulent properties on global stellar parameters. Using 2D O-star models, we studied several statistical properties of the turbulence that develops in these models. We compute autocorrelation functions of density and velocity to study typical eddy length scales. Moreover, we compute kinetic energy power spectra to analyze the energy distribution and compare this to known results from established turbulence theories. We find anisotropy of the turbulent eddies in velocity space. Moreover, this anisotropy increases with classical Eddington factor. This anisotropy disappears in density space where all models show nearly isotropic structures and no dependence on stellar parameters. The kinetic energy power spectra exhibit an inertial range with a cascade exponent that has an average value of -2.57. This exponent does not show any clear dependence on stellar parameters. Importantly, this energy cascade is significantly steeper than those in known turbulence theories such as Kolmogorov turbulence with exponent -5/3 and Burgers turbulence with exponent -2. This additional steepening can potentially be attributed to radiative damping which increases with increasing wavenumber. Sub-surface turbulence in hot, massive stars is anisotropic and radially dominated in velocity space and its energy cascade is steeper than both Kolmogorov turbulence and Burgers turbulence. Although not rigorously proven here, we suggest that this steepening is due to the scale-dependent effect of radiative damping.

entries.title: Magnetic kink instability of jet-wind outflows. I. Static column configuration
entries.abstract: We describe the results of computer simulations investigating the stability of an axisymmetric static equilibrium combining a highly magnetised ($σ=10^3$) central column and a mildly ($σ=0.1$) to weakly ($σ=0.001$) magnetised outer shell with a helical and mostly force-free magnetic field of constant pitch. The measured linear growth rates of the instability are in agreement with the maximum growth rate for a uniform density column with a force-free magnetic field of constant pitch obtained by Appl et al. (2000), being only a little bit higher. At the non-linear phase, the interface separating the central column and the outer shell develops the characteristic corkscrew shape, with the space inside and between the coils of the corkscrew filled by the shell plasma. In high-resolution runs, a secondary instability is seen as well. It has the form of helical protuberances of low-$σ$ plasma intruding inside the corkscrew coils. These appear to be aligned with the local magnetic field lines. We tentatively identify the secondary instability as the magnetic Rayleigh-Taylor instability. Overall, the results indicate that the current-driven kink instability may provide the baryon-loading of AGN jets suggested by the observations.

entries.title: Extending an X-ray & Mid-Infrared diagnostic for absorption in Active Galactic Nuclei to higher redshifts using NuSTAR and XMM-Newton
entries.abstract: Determining the Compton thick fraction ($f_{CT}$) within the population of Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN) provides insight into the evolution and growth of Supermassive Black Holes. Measuring $f_{CT}$ requires methods of modelling the AGN column density ($N_{\mathrm{H}}$), typically through spectral fitting which requires high source counts, or estimation methods such as the band ratio. We extend an $N_{\mathrm{H}}$ estimation method using the ratio of observed X-ray and MIR luminosity ($\log\left({L}_{2-10\mathrm{keV}} / {L}_{12\mathrm{μm}}\right)$), previously applied in the local universe ($z<0.1$), to a higher redshift. We used a sample of 47 bright AGN from the NuSTAR 80-month catalogue (NSS80) with a median redshift of $\langle z \rangle = 0.35$ as the high redshift comparison, and we applied X-ray spectral fitting to the NuSTAR sources with physically motivated AGN models to provide $N_\mathrm{H}$ constraints. The high-$z$ relationship was found to be consistent with the same model as the low-$z$ comparison, but with modestly different parameters which we determined to be due to a higher X-ray luminosity within the NSS80 sample. We applied the model to the full NSS80 catalogue to determine a statistical measure of the observed Compton thick fraction at $f_{CT}=4.9^{+2.0}_{-2.3}\%$ to $1σ$ uncertainty, consistent with other recent low-$z$ Swift/BAT measurements.

entries.title: Zeeman-Doppler imaging of V889 Her: Surface spots and magnetic field topology 2017 - 2023
entries.abstract: The surface magnetic field of the young solar analogue V889 Her is studied using Zeeman-Doppler imaging (ZDI). This well-studied star has previously been reported to have an exceptionally high differential rotation and show abrupt changes in the surface magnetic field and spot configuration. Our aim is to study the evolution of the magnetic field topology in V889 Her. This will contribute to understanding dynamo action in young solar-type stars. We also want to constrain the surface differential rotation curve of the target star.Methods. We employ the ZDI method on observations collected with the SOFIN spectropolarimeter mounted at the Nordic Optical Telescope. We test differential rotation parameters previously reported in studies of the star. We observe significant changes in the radial field near the rotational pole throughout the whole span of the observations. Specifically, the polarity of the radial field is reversed around 2021. The large-scale magnetic field also contains a persistent strong azimuthal component at high latitudes. We detect abrupt changes in the spot configuration in June 2018 on the time scale of a week. The observations favour a solar type differential rotation. The different rotation parameters influence the brightness map more than the magnetic field topology. We cannot link the observed changes in the magnetic field topology with the evolution of the long-term spot activity. The abrupt changes observed in 2018 confirm previous reports that the surface magnetic field and spot configuration may undergo rapid evolution on short time scales. This complicates the estimation of the surface differential rotation.

entries.title: A Multiscale Analysis of an Interplanetary Shock from IMAP, SOLAR-1, and the L1 Constellation to Earth
entries.abstract: Collisionless shocks are primary sites of particle acceleration throughout the Universe. Transient, mesoscale structures forming around these shocks influence their energy conversion efficiency, yet remain poorly observed at interplanetary (IP) shocks: spacecraft sample the shock transition briefly, and single-point measurements cannot disentangle temporal evolution from spatial structure. Here, we examine a fast, CME-driven IP shock of 2026 January 19, observed by IMAP, SOLAR-1, Wind, ACE, DSCOVR, and Aditya-L1 at L1 and by ARTEMIS and MMS near Earth, to determine its spatial and temporal structure. At MHD scales, a pre-existing solar wind flux tube is overtaken by the shock as it crosses the L1 fleet. This inflates the apparent magnetic compression ratio far beyond the ideal strong-shock limit of 4, showing that upstream and downstream intervals can sample different plasma and bias single-spacecraft estimates. At kinetic scales, IMAP and SOLAR-1, separated by only $\sim$7 $R_E$ ($\sim$340 ion inertial lengths), sample the same foreshock yet record localized structures that differ measurably; these are the first candidate signatures of large-scale foreshock transients at an IP shock. Further upstream, shocklets appear hundreds of $R_E$ ahead of the shock, consistent with steepening of ambient solar wind waves. Near Earth, the shock-to-flux-tube arrival lag increases to approximately six minutes, corresponding to a nominal sheath extension of $\sim$50 $R_E$, indicating sheath expansion over $\sim$200 $R_E$ of propagation. Together, these results show that the IP shock, its foreshock, and its sheath evolve across multiple scales from L1 to Earth, underscoring the need for multipoint measurements to resolve the underlying processes.

entries.title: Density fluctuations in pseudo-streamer and helmet streamer: Generation, propagation and comparison with Metis observations
entries.abstract: Recent white-light observations from the Metis coronagraph on board Solar Orbiter have shown the presence of propagating density fluctuations with a period of $\sim5$ minutes, particularly in the observationally bright regions of helmet streamers and pseudo-streamers. These density fluctuations have been shown to originate from magnetohydrodynamic wave modes -- slow and fast modes can directly compress the plasma, whereas Alfvén waves generate density fluctuations via a non-linear coupling with the slow and fast modes. In general, in low plasma $β$ regions, slow modes contribute more towards the generation of density fluctuations, whereas in high $β$ regions, there are significant contributions from both slow and fast waves. In this work, we investigate the propagation of (non-linear) Alfvén waves and the associated density fluctuations using a 2.5D axisymmetric global solar wind model that includes two distinct magnetic field topologies -- a helmet streamer and a pseudo-streamer. Key differences in these magnetic configurations give rise to differences in the wave behaviour due to, for example, the presence of a current sheet in the helmet streamer and an X-type null point in the pseudo-streamer, and the structure of the $β= 1$ layer in both magnetic field configurations. This leads to the possible creation of prominent interference patterns along the helmet streamer axis, which do not appear along the pseudo-streamer axis. Unlike in the streamer region, we also find that along the pseudo-streamer axis, the contribution to the density fluctuations is due to the fast waves only, despite being in a low $β$ plasma.

entries.title: A New Galactic Close Binary Supersoft Source Candidate
entries.abstract: The identification of a new galactic Close Binary Supersoft Source (CBSS) candidate, whose main ID is ZTF J043609.49+364057.7, is presented on the basis of the analysis of its optical spectrum, light curve and Spectral Energy Distribution (SED). During a survey designed to find candidates to the aforementioned class independently of X-ray emissions, this object's optical spectrum was found to exhibit the typical emission features expected for a CBSS. The available photometric data show a quasi-sinusoidal modulation, with a period of 5.42 h, compatible with the orbital modulation of the system. Although there is no current identification of X-ray emission from this source, its SED displays a highly absorbed bright FUV component, given the estimated E(B - V) ~ 0.7 mag.

analysis.reason: The paper uses GW polarization as an absolute compass for lens-induced orientations of BNS jet images. That is a strong-lensing measurement method, not a substantial result on jet physics, FRBs, supernova engines, shocks, CSM interaction, or neutrinos.
analysis.result: GW polarization is an absolute reference for intrinsic jet orientation: its offset from the apparent jet axis is the lens-induced orientation offset of each image. Images obey $\boldsymbol{\beta}=\boldsymbol{\theta}-\nabla\Psi$ at stationary points of $\tau(\boldsymbol{\theta};\boldsymbol{\beta})=\frac{1}{2}|\boldsymbol{\theta}-\boldsymbol{\beta}|^2-\Psi$, with $\mu_j=1/\det A_j$ and $\Delta\chi_j\equiv\chi_j-\psi\pmod{\pi}$. After ET+CE selection the detected images are 93% doubles, 5% quadruples, and 2% triples (5908 systems; median $z_s=2.3$, median $\theta_E=0.63''$, longest delay 48 days). Median $\sigma_z/(1+z_s)=0.04$, 27% have $\sigma_\psi<10^\circ$, offsets reach tens of degrees, and at most about one third are measurable; quadrupole $\psi$ is useful only for viewing angles $\gtrsim40^\circ$.
analysis.problem: Strongly lensed GW images are one-dimensional time series without sky positions, while a resolvable BNS jet does not reveal its intrinsic orientation, so electromagnetic data usually constrain only relative orientations between images.
analysis.method: A static thin lens parallel-transports polarization so $\psi$ is invariant. Three image-plane layers use host-arc positions, Fermat delays and magnifications, and $\chi_j=\arg[A_j^{-1}\hat{e}(\chi_s)]\pmod{\pi}$, with $\sigma_{\Delta\chi,j}^2=\sigma_\psi^2+\sigma_{\chi,j}^2+\sigma_\epsilon^2$ and detection when $\max_j S_j\ge3$. Mock BNS events use flat $\Lambda$CDM, a semi-analytic galaxy lens, and a joint nonspinning 3.5PN TaylorF2 Fisher analysis on ET+CE.

analysis.reason: FRB 20240114A shows a roughly 120 day modulation of its linear polarization fraction, directly constraining emission geometry versus magneto-ionic propagation for a repeating FRB.
analysis.result: Daily-mean DOL periodograms peak near 120 days: phase-distance correlation reaches 0.1452 at $P=119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ (99% global threshold 0.1262; $3\sigma$ interval $119.91^{+2.67}_{-2.04}\,\mathrm{d}$), and generalized Lomb–Scargle reaches power 0.1275 at $122.31\,\mathrm{d}$ (threshold 0.1108; interval $122.31^{+2.63}_{-2.82}\,\mathrm{d}$). Daily medians peak at $119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ and $123.55\,\mathrm{d}$, with global FAPs $5.71\times10^{-4}$ and $2.84\times10^{-3}$ (about $3.25\sigma$ and $2.77\sigma$). Folding at $119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ gives semi-amplitude 3.23% (peak-to-peak 6.46%). For $P_{\rm orb}=119.91\,\mathrm{d}$ and $M_{\rm tot}=10M_\odot$, $a\simeq1.03\,\mathrm{au}$. For 18 bright bursts, $\sigma_{\rm RM}<0.51\,\mathrm{rad\,m^{-2}}$ (95%), so $p_{\rm L}=p_{\rm L,0}\exp[-2\sigma_{\rm RM}^2\lambda^4]$ lowers DOL by only about 0.42% and 0.083% at 1.0 and 1.5 GHz. With $I=10^{45}\,\mathrm{g\,cm^2}$ and $P_{\rm spin}=120\,\mathrm{d}$, $E_{\rm rot}\simeq1.84\times10^{32}\,\mathrm{erg}$, far below $E_{\rm iso}\sim10^{37}$–$10^{39}\,\mathrm{erg}$.

analysis.problem: Whether the degree of linear polarization of repeating FRB 20240114A varies periodically over hundreds of days, and whether that variation traces emission geometry or propagation through a changing circumburst or binary environment.
analysis.method: After S/N$>20$, 6099 bursts on 95 days spanning MJD 60337.238–60824.896 ($T=487.66\,\mathrm{d}$) are averaged without weights into daily DOL. Trials from 10 to 240 days use $\Delta f=1/(\mathrm{OS}\,T)$ with $\mathrm{OS}=200$ ($\Delta f\approx1.025\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{d}^{-1}$; 9348 frequencies). PDC correlates $a_{ij}=|D_i-D_j|$ with $b_{ij}(P)=\phi_{ij}(P)[P-\phi_{ij}(P)]$; GLS fits $D(t)=C+a\cos(2\pi ft)+b\sin(2\pi ft)$ and uses $\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{GLS}}(f)=1-\mathrm{RSS}(f)/\mathrm{RSS}_0$. Global significance uses $10^7$ permutations on fixed dates, $\mathrm{FAP}_{\mathrm{global}}=(r+1)/(M+1)$. Phase folding uses $\phi_i=\mathrm{mod}((t_i-t_0)/P,1)$ and $\mathrm{DOL}(\phi)=C+a\cos(2\pi\phi)+b\sin(2\pi\phi)$.
assumptions: A single external screen obeying the Burn relation $p_{\rm L}=p_{\rm L,0}\exp[-2\sigma_{\rm RM}^2\lambda^4]$ is the propagation model tested against the DOL modulation.
limits: A single external screen obeying the Burn relation cannot reproduce the full fitted DOL variation, and the $\sigma_{\rm RM}$ bound applies only to 18 selected bright broadband bursts rather than every long-period phase.

Class I distinct bursts give the delay-corrected span $L_{ijkl}=|(t_{jl}-t_{ik})-(\Delta_j-\Delta_i)|/(1+z_s)$; Class II same-burst images encode only the lens delay. The rate model is $r(s)=\lambda_0\mathbf{1}_{[b,b+T_{\mathrm{act}})}(s)$, with expected counts $\mu_X=\nu_0\int a_X(s)\,ds$ and $\nu_0=8766\lambda_0$, sampled in $P_{\mathrm{sid}}=86164\,\mathrm{s}$ windows.
assumptions: An effective single-plane potential is used for MACS J0717.5+3745 at $z_l=0.54$ in a flat cosmology with $H_0=70\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$ and $\Omega_{\mathrm{m}0}=0.3$.

analysis.reason: This FAST UMAP–HDBSCAN study of FRB 20121102A directly tests whether repeating bursts form emission subclasses whose mix changes between active episodes. The drop of the high-energy Cluster 1 from about 27% to about 8% is relevant to FRB radiation conditions and source environment.
analysis.result: HDBSCAN finds four clusters plus noise. Cluster 1 contains nearly all high-energy bursts, has a mean energy about one order of magnitude higher, shows bimodal central frequency and bandwidth, and occupies a separate width–flux region. Its fractions are $26.9^{+2.3}_{-2.2}\%$ (2019), $7.7^{+3.1}_{-2.3}\%$ (2022), and $7.8^{+6.4}_{-3.7}\%$ (2023). Clusters 2 and 4 have mean bandwidth ratios $\sim 0.1$ at higher and lower central frequencies, respectively; Cluster 3 has larger bandwidth and bandwidth ratio. All clusters have bandwidth ratio $<0.4$ and similar bimodal waiting times. Relative to $T_{\mathrm{B,cri}}\approx 10^{33}\,\mathrm{K}$, Cluster 1 contains most classical bursts. In the condensed tree, $\lambda=1/d$ and Cluster 1 separates near $\lambda\sim 0.3$. A curvature-radiation reading uses $\nu_{\rm c}\propto\gamma^{3}/\rho$.
analysis.problem: Whether repeat bursts of FRB 20121102A contain subclasses associated with different radiation mechanisms or emission-region conditions, and whether those subclass fractions change across the 2019, 2022, and 2023 active episodes.
analysis.method: FAST samples of 1652, 431, and 124 bursts are compared above a common threshold $E\geq 2.5\times 10^{37}\,\mathrm{erg}$. The silhouette score $s(o_i)=(b(o_i)-a(o_i))/\max\{a(o_i),b(o_i)\}$ selects $n_{\rm neighbors}=7$, min_dist $=0.0$, min_cluster_size $=200$, and min_samples $=10$.
